overnightPermit.where: Camping is on unregulated Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest and private timberland; no wilderness permit or registration is needed. The Dailey Prairie logging-road gate is separately locked to vehicles by the timber company, which is an access issue unrelated to camping.

overnightPermit.what: North Cascades National Park wilderness permit, required once past Hannegan Pass into the Chilliwack valley — quota, not free
overnightPermit.where: Reserve on Recreation.gov, especially for the popular Copper Ridge/Chilliwack corridor; the park increasingly issues reserved permits by email after a mandatory safety video rather than an in-person pickup. The short stretch on the Mount Baker-Snoqualmie side above Hannegan Camp needs a separate, free, self-issue Mount Baker Wilderness permit at the trailhead.

overnightPermit.what: North Cascades National Park wilderness permit for Boston Basin and Sahale Glacier Camp — quota, reservable, not free
overnightPermit.where: Both are high-demand cross-country zones; apply to the March early-access lottery for the best odds, or book the general on-sale release in late April on Recreation.gov. Permits reached from Cascade River Road must be picked up in person at the Wilderness Information Center in Marblemount.

This is general Okanogan-Wenatchee National Forest land outside any wilderness boundary; parties bivy informally at the trailhead or a highway pullout. A Northwest Forest Pass or day-use fee is needed to park, and no camping is allowed within a quarter mile of Blue Lake itself.

overnightPermit.what: Olympic National Park wilderness permit — reservable, not free
overnightPermit.where: Book on Recreation.gov; $8 per person per night plus a $6 reservation fee, or cover it with an annual Olympic Wilderness Pass. Summer-season reservations open in mid-April.
